When human life lay foully for all to see, crushed to the earth under heavy religion…

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with De Rerum Natura I.62–63, within the tradition of Epicureanism. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of fear, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Lucretius's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
